comment: This passage explains that the foundational capabilities are interdependent - a longitudinal record has little weight without the registries that establish provenance and attribution. The financing chapter does not draw the consequence: if value arises from interdependence, it cannot be measured component by component, so component-level appraisal will reliably under-invest in the foundation.

public.text: This passage explains that the foundational capabilities are interdependent - a longitudinal record has little weight without the registries that establish provenance and attribution. The financing chapter does not draw the consequence: if value arises from interdependence, it cannot be measured component by component, so component-level appraisal will reliably under-invest in the foundation.
public.suggestedRevision: State explicitly that the value of DPI-H is emergent from the interdependence described here, and draw the financing consequence in 4.6.1: appraisal should be at the level of the shared foundation rather than the individual component, which is a further argument for recurrent budget lines over project appraisal. This also answers a question the draft leaves open - why health technology with demonstrated value often still fails to be financed.
